Article Title: US government bans American technology company from Green Card programme for two years; fines $1.4 million; DOJ says: Violated Immigration and Nationality Act by …
Article Text:
US government bans American technology company from Green Card programme for two years; fines $1.4 million; DOJ says: Violated Immigration and Nationality Act by …

"Cloudera will establish a back-pay fund of $1.4 million to compensate qualified U.S. workers who tried to apply for the jobs at issue but were not given fair consideration. Cloudera also will pay $600,000 in civil penalties to the United States,"

What the Justice department said banning Cloudera from PERM

US government has banned Cloudera, a Santa Clara, California-based data management company from participating in the Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) program for two years. For those unaware, PERM is the required first step for US employers to sponsor a foreign worker for a permanent employment-based green card. In a press release, the Department of Justice said that it has imposed a fine of $1.4 million on Cloudera Cloudera for violating the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) by discriminating against U.S. workers when recruiting and hiring for seven positions under the PERM process.the department said.“There are no exceptions: the Justice Department will hold accountable employers who discriminate against U.S. workers,” said Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K.Dhillon of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division. “This substantial settlement, in partnership with DOL, sends a strong signal to employers that the federal government will work together to ensure employers treat U.S. workers fairly. ”The debarment follows DOL’s earlier suspension of Cloudera’s PERM processing and reflects DOL’s commitment to aggressively enforcing labor certification requirements when employers fail to provide US workers a fair opportunity to compete for jobs.In the official release, DOJ said:“The U.S. Department of Justice’s Civil Rights Division (CRT) and the U.S. Department of Labor (DOL) today announced a coordinated enforcement resolution with Cloudera Inc., a Santa Clara, California-based data management company, following allegations that the company discriminated against qualified U.S. workers during recruitment conducted under the Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) program.“There are no exceptions: the Justice Department will hold accountable employers who discriminate against U.S. workers,” said Assistant Attorney General Harmeet K. Dhillon of the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division. “This substantial settlement, in partnership with DOL, sends a strong signal to employers that the federal government will work together to ensure employers treat U.S. workers fairly. ”As part of the resolution, Cloudera will be barred from participating in the PERM program for two years, one of the most significant sanctions available for DOL to protect the integrity of the employment-based immigration system and safeguard opportunities for U.S. workers. The debarment follows DOL’s earlier suspension of Cloudera’s PERM processing and reflects DOL’s commitment to aggressively enforcing labor certification requirements when employers fail to provide U.S. workers a fair opportunity to compete for jobs.The settlement also resolves a lawsuit DOJ filed in April of this year, alleging that Cloudera violated the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) by discriminating against U.S. workers when recruiting and hiring for seven positions under the PERM process. Under the terms of the settlement with the Justice Department, Cloudera will establish a back-pay fund of $1.4 million to compensate qualified U.S. workers who tried to apply for the jobs at issue but were not given fair consideration. Cloudera also will pay $600,000 in civil penalties to the United States.In addition to the two-year debarment, Cloudera will be subject to compliance obligations designed to ensure future adherence to federal labor and anti-discrimination laws. These measures include enhanced monitoring, revised PERM compliance procedures, and reporting requirements intended to prevent future violations.This debarment and compliance framework establish an important enforcement precedent and strengthen future efforts to protect U.S. workers. The PERM program allows employers to sponsor aliens for permanent residence only after demonstrating that qualified U.S. workers were provided a genuine opportunity to apply and that no qualified, willing, and available U.S. workers could be found. Employers who evade these requirements undermine both program integrity and the interests of U.S. workers. This resolution is one of many examples of coordinated federal enforcement designed to ensure employers comply with labor market protections established by Congress.This settlement is also the fourteenth settlement since DOJ re-launched its Protecting U.S. Workers Initiative in 2025 to enforce the INA’s prohibition on citizenship status discrimination against companies that illegally discriminate against U.S. workers in favor of those with temporary employment visas. Under these settlements, DOJ obtains civil penalties for each violation and will continue to appropriately seek the maximum penalty permitted by law. The settlements also involve awards of back pay, when warranted, and require employers to conduct comprehensive training for relevant staff and recruiters and cease restricting consideration for job opportunities based on workers’ citizenship status without a lawful reason."
Article Summary: US government has banned Cloudera, a Santa Clara, California-based data management company, from participating in the Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) program for two years. PERM is the required first step for US employers to sponsor a foreign worker for a permanent employment-based green card. DOJ said that it has imposed a fine of $1.4 million on Clou dera for violating the Immigration and Nationality Act.

Article Title: Meta AI head Alexandr Wang praises Mark Zuckerberg, he replies: I have never gotten such a nice…
Article Text:
Mark Zuckerberg and Alexandr Wang

‘ Very Bayesian ’: Rapid decisive conviction

Meta AI head Alexandr Wang and company CEO Mark Zuckerberg recently had a candid exchange on the company's executive leadership and high-stakes decision-making. During a recent interview, Meta’s Wang was asked about the qualities of Facebook founder, and he offered glowing praise for Zuckerberg, highlighting his exceptional willingness to make massive, rapid pivots based on core convictions. During the conversation Wang was specifically asked how Zuckerberg differed as a leader from what he initially anticipated. Before Wang could reply, Zuckerberg opened with a lighthearted quip, joking, “I think I can leave now.” Wang quickly followed up with his perspective on their working relationship over the past year.Wang noted that while he does not have an extensive set of comparisons, observing Zuckerberg's management style firsthand revealed unique traits that stand out even within elite tech founder circles:“One of the very cool things about working with Mark over the past year has just been watching the true degree of his boldness,” Wang explained, adding, “Once he internalises certain beliefs, like the speed and magnitude of willing to change prior actions and pivot towards the worldview that is consistent with those beliefs, I think these are pretty unusual traits, generally speaking, even among this base of founders. Very Bayesian.”The analytical praise drew a warm, humorous reaction from Zuckerberg.“Very Bayesian. I've never gotten such a nice compliment,” Zuckerberg responded.A person who follows the Bayesian method relies on statistical inference, using Bayes' theorem to update the probability of a hypothesis as new data or evidence becomes available.Expanding on his observations, Wang admitted that Zuckerberg's appetite for sweeping strategic gambles initially took him by surprise before earning his deep respect.“No, but then I think also just the degree of boldness. It was actually quite puzzling to me at first, the degree to which you were willing to make these massive bets. That is quite a notable trait and something I really admire,” Wang continued.Zuckerberg concluded the exchange with appreciation for the assessment, replying: “I'm so flattered.”
Article Summary: Meta AI head Alexandr Wang and Facebook CEO Mark Zuckerberg recently had a candid exchange on the company's executive leadership and high-stakes decision- making. Wang noted that observing Zuckerberg's management style firsthand revealed unique traits that stand out even within elite tech founder circles.

Article Title: Boat expands global footprint with Sri Lanka, Bhutan launch; international revenue surges in FY26
Article Text: Homegrown audio and wearables brand Boat has expanded its international presence with its entry into Sri Lanka and Bhutan, as the company looks to accelerate growth beyond India under its "Boat 2.0" strategy. The company said its international revenue more than doubled in FY26, a performance it described as an early validation of its efforts to build markets outside India. The latest expansion strengthens Boat's footprint across South Asia, Southeast Asia and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region.Boat will launch a multi-category portfolio in both Sri Lanka and Bhutan, covering personal audio products, smartwatches and charging solutions. The company said it plans to tailor its offerings over time based on local consumer preferences and market demand.The move comes as Boat seeks to diversify its growth drivers after establishing itself as a leading player in India's audio and wearables market. International markets are expected to play a key role in the company's next phase of growth, alongside expansion into newer consumer technology categories.According to Boat, Sri Lanka and Bhutan offer attractive opportunities due to their young, increasingly digital-first populations, rising adoption of personal electronics and familiarity with Indian brands and popular culture. Commenting on the expansion, Gaurav Nayyar, CEO of Boat, said the company's international strategy is focused on building relevance market by market rather than simply expanding product availability."For us, international expansion is not about putting the same products on more shelves. It is about building market by market, understanding local consumers and creating relevance in each geography," Nayyar said.He added that the company aims to build Boat into a global lifestyle technology brand originating from India, competing on product design, innovation and consumer understanding.The international push comes amid a broader evolution of Boat's business. While audio remains its core category, the company said it has expanded its capabilities in wearables, charging solutions and other emerging technology segments. It added that its wearables business turned profitable in FY26, while charging solutions and other emerging categories contributed a growing share of profits.Supporting the expansion is Boat Labs, the company's in-house research and development centre, which employs more than 100 engineers focused on product development and innovation across categories.Going forward, Boat said it plans to deepen its presence in existing overseas markets while evaluating further expansion opportunities across South Asia, Southeast Asia, the GCC and other high-potential regions.
Article Summary: Boat will launch a multi-category portfolio in both Sri Lanka and Bhutan. The company said it plans to tailor its offerings over time based on local consumer preferences and market demand. The move comes as Boat seeks to diversify its growth drivers after establishing itself as a leading player in India's audio and wearables market.

Article Title: Microsoft says AI agents inside companies can’t be trusted, wants ‘Guardian Agents’ to watch their moves
Article Text:
Guarding the companies with ‘Guardian Agents’

At a time when there is a growing wave of publicly disclosed safety incidents highlighting the sheer power and potential hazards of modern artificial intelligence (AI) and AI agents, cybersecurity experts are sounding the alarm on an overlooked vulnerability: the autonomous software agents operating inside corporate networks. While the broader tech industry has remained fixated on external cybercriminals weaponizing models, companies have quietly deployed thousands of internal agents to handle everyday business processes. Microsoft says that since these agents were implemented internally, organisations have largely treated them with implicit trust, there is a need for ‘Guardian Agents’ to make matters more secure.When optimised purely to attain targets, AI models are prone to reward hacking – cutting corners or finding unintended loopholes that violate organisational judgment and unwritten business norms. And as the global race for innovation accelerates, these containment challenges will only multiply as underlying models become more capable.To prevent agentic insiders from triggering enterprise disruptions, security professionals argue that oversight must be continuous, real-time and pre-emptive.An autonomous agent combines a frontier model, an orchestration harness, an assigned action space of tools, and an execution runtime.Defending this footprint requires security controls spanning identity, permissions, data layers, endpoints, networks and cloud runtimes. Guardian Agents are an established industry mechanism where dedicated supervisory models monitor and moderate every planned action of every operational agent 24/7, before that action is actually executed.First announced by Microsoft in July to help cyber defenders outpace AI-driven attacks originating outside corporate walls, Project Perception is now being directed inward to oversee and govern internal agentic insiders. Built to impose deterministic controls on non-deterministic artificial intelligence, the platform uses a multi-layered cyber architecture.It gathers telemetry across identity, data, endpoints, network, and runtime environments to identify untracked agents in the enterprise; evaluates incoming telemetry in real time to calculate the exact risk profile of what an agent is trying to accomplish and then uses collaborative teams of Guardian, “green,” and “blue” agents to supervise actions around the clock.By pairing algorithmic speed with human oversight, security practitioners gain complete traceability to investigate what happened, analyze why a risk surfaced, and exercise human judgment to calibrate security rules.
Article Summary: Microsoft says that since these agents were implemented internally, organisations have largely treated them with implicit trust. There is a need for ‘Guardian Agents’ to make matters more secure. When optimised purely to attain targets, AI models are prone to reward hacking – cutting corners or finding unintended loopholes.

Article Title: Disney made Character.AI file for bankruptcy before buying its tech, court filings show
Article Text:
FILE PHOTO_ Illustration shows Disney+ logo (Reuters)

Disney's Character.AI deal began weeks before the bankruptcy filing

Character.AI's lawsuits and state probes stay behind with the startup

Character.AI's bankruptcy filing last week looked like the end of a struggling AI startup. Court documents now suggest it was part of a plan. According to filings reviewed by Wired, Disney required its deal with the chatbot company to be completed through Chapter 11 proceedings, pointing to Character.AI's shrinking cash reserves and the legal and regulatory risks piling up around it.That structure lets Disney take most of Character.AI's employees and a wide licence to its technology, while the lawsuits and state investigations stay with the startup. Character.AI, which has around 12 million active users and has been losing $8 million to $9 million a month, filed for bankruptcy in a Delaware court on October 12.The filings describe two linked transactions. The first happened in September, when Disney paid Character.AI $5.5 million and put down a refundable $2 million deposit. It also hired the majority of the startup's staff, including then-CEO Karandeep Anand, who is now Disney's first chief technology officer. Some of those hires will help keep Character.AI running for five months.The second stage plays out in bankruptcy court. Disney is the stalking-horse bidder for a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive licence to Character.AI's code and tools, from its trust and safety moderation stack to its training infrastructure and age-prediction technology.User data and the website are not part of it.If Disney wins the auction, it pays another $12.5 million at closing, taking the total to about $20 million. If a rival outbids it, Disney gets its deposit back plus a breakup fee. Disney has also offered jobs to at least 60 employees, with annual pay estimated at $60 million.Disney has also drafted what the filings call a "363 Free and Clear Order". If approved, it would establish that the deal is not a merger and that Character.AI alone stays responsible for its liabilities, including legal claims.That matters because the claims are serious. A multistate investigation into the company has grown to 46 states and territories, and a filing on behalf of 40 of them cites chatbot screenshots encouraging minors to hide self-harm injuries and kill their parents. Character.AI says the filing misrepresents the safety of its platform.Wired describes the arrangement as a new twist on the "reverse acquihire", where a company takes a startup's talent and technology without formally buying it. John Newman, a University of Memphis law professor and former deputy director at the Federal Trade Commission's competition bureau, told the publication that existing corporate law safeguards were never designed for a deal like this. "It's bad for society to let companies exercise control without responsibility," he said.The states have reserved the right to challenge any bankruptcy plan, so the question of who answers for Character.AI's chatbots could still be fought out in court before Disney gets its licence. The sale is expected to close by late November or early December. Disney declined to comment.
Article Summary: Disney's Character.AI deal began weeks before the bankruptcy filing. Disney's lawsuits and state probes stay behind with the startup. Disney is the stalking- horse bidder for a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive licence to Character. AI's code and tools.

Article Title: Google DeepMind’s AI wins another game, company says Gemini 4 Argon agents beat Minecraft from scratch in 27 hours
Article Text:
Google DeepMind

Why the ‘ Minecraft Grand Challenge ’ matters for real-world AI

Harvest and process raw materials,

Venture into dangerous alternate dimensions to secure rare resources,

Use spatial mathematics to locate a hidden underground fortress, and

Eliminate a flying boss monster that continuously regenerates health.

Any misstep can lead to death, stripping the player of inventory and forcing hours of recovery.

Google DeepMind has achieved another major gaming benchmark, announcing that a team of four autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) agents powered by its new Gemini 4 Argon model successfully completed Minecraft from scratch in just 27 hours. Unlike DeepMind's historic gaming breakthroughs, such as AlphaGo and AlphaStar, which relied on systems custom-trained specifically for a single title, the latest feat was accomplished using general-purpose coding agents – the identical software assistants engineers deploy for daily programming tasks.Operating inside a sandboxed survival world with human oversight limited strictly to safety monitoring, the four AI agents wrote code in real time, coordinated division of labor via text chat and debugged thousands of errors without any pre-programmed game logic or human intervention. Twenty-seven hours and 2,783 custom programs later, the team conquered the game by slaying its final boss, the Ender Dragon.“Four Gemini 4 Argon agents beat Minecraft from scratch in 27 hours. Operating in a sandbox using only code and text, they wrote 2,783 programs, divided up jobs over chat, shared notes, and debugged errors together - all with no human help,” Google DeepMind said.Completing Minecraft in a randomly generated survival world represents one of the steepest tests in computer science because it requires maintaining a long-term, coherent operational plan across thousands of dependent, high-stakes tasks. Players must:While earlier community tests achieved partial runs by relying on shortcuts, such as running on peaceful mode, exploring pre-scouted maps, starting with active portals, or using hard-coded game scripts, DeepMind sought to test whether standard coding models could accomplish the entire journey unaided, armed only with their general training data and a bare code interface.According to DeepMind, demonstrating that autonomous agents can collaborate, rebound from repeated failures, and stick to a multi-day objective proves they can tackle the open-ended problem solving required for cutting-edge software engineering, scientific research, robotics, and complex physical systems.Thirty-nine minutes after destroying the final healing crystal, the agents brought down the dragon. The decisive final blow was struck by a surviving agent clinging to just 2.5 out of 20 health points.
Article Summary: Google DeepMind's Gemini 4 Argon team completed the game in just 27 hours. Four AI agents wrote code in real time, coordinated division of labor via text chat and debugged thousands of errors without any pre-programmed game logic or human intervention. The team conquered the game by slaying its final boss, the Ender Dragon.

Article Title: Microsoft says AI agents should start with zero access, unveils new security controls
Article Text:
Why agents are an insider risk

What Microsoft is adding

An example: the expense agent

“Customer Zero”

Microsoft has announced a set of new security tools aimed at treating AI agents as a new kind of insider risk, with controls designed to limit what each agent can access and to tighten those limits automatically if its behaviour changes. The announcement was made in a blog post by Nadim Abdo, corporate vice president of identity and network access at Microsoft. It extends Project Perception, Microsoft’s agentic security system introduced earlier this year, to cover the agents that companies are deploying across their operations.Abdo said agents are quickly becoming part of how work gets done, from writing code and analysing revenue to processing expenses. To be useful, they often need access to company data, applications and tools, and that access creates insider risk.He stressed that this doesn’t mean agents are inherently malicious. They can make mistakes, be manipulated or be compromised, he said, and an agent that behaves as intended at the start of a task can act differently as its context changes. They can also run continuously at machine speed and scale.Abdo cited remarks by Microsoft chairman and CEO Satya Nadella, who has argued that security controls must sit outside the AI model, where it can’t bypass or tamper with them.“The most trustworthy agentic system will not be the one with the model we trust most,” Nadella said. “It will be the one designed that enables us to trust the model least.”The company framed its approach around four tasks: know which agents exist, contain what they can do, protect the data and systems in their path, and adapt protection as risk changes. The main new features include:* Wider agent discovery. Microsoft is adding 35 types of local agents, bringing the total supported to 60, including Claude Code, OpenAI Codex and GitHub Copilot. Companies can bring them into one registry to see who owns them and what they are doing.* Agent identities. Microsoft Entra Agent ID will add identity types for more agent patterns, including local and previously unknown agents found by security sensors. This is meant to let companies tell what a person did apart from what an agent did on that person’s behalf.* Dynamic Permissions. Agents would start with no authority and receive only what an approved task needs, for only as long as it takes. Organisation-wide policy sets the outer limit, and higher-impact actions can require verified human approval.* Dynamic Agent Risk. A continuously updated risk assessment combining signals from identity, data, endpoints, cloud, network, runtime and the agent’s own activity. It considers whether an agent’s actions are drifting from the intent of its user or organisation.* Dynamic Conditional Access. An extension of Entra Conditional Access for agents. When risk rises, policy can respond in steps: reduce permissions, allow reads but block writes, narrow the resources an agent can reach, require human approval, or isolate the agent and stop it.* Guardian Agents and Playbooks. A team of agents inside Project Perception that investigates why risk changed and recommends or applies containment. People set policy, approval limits and delegation rules.* Model-level evidence. Microsoft plans to feed signals such as chain-of-thought into its risk scoring to spot when an agent’s plans diverge from its task. It said security decisions must remain independent of the model.* Sandboxed runtime. Sandboxes such as Microsoft Execution Container give agents policy-controlled access to resources, so a compromised agent cannot switch off the controls watching it.Abdo illustrated the approach with an expense-approval agent that can read submissions, check policy and approve routine reimbursements, but does not inherit all of its sponsoring employee’s access. If it hits a prompt injection in an outside document or attempts an unrelated action, its risk score rises. Policy could then keep read access, remove the ability to approve or write, block sensitive resources and require provable human approval. If the risk keeps climbing, the system could isolate or stop the agent.Terrell Cox, Microsoft’s corporate vice president and deputy chief information security officer for customer security, said the company is already operating with hundreds of thousands of agents. “Agents will only be adopted at scale if they can be trusted at scale,” he said, adding that Microsoft’s experience as “Customer Zero” informs the new tools.Abdo wrote that the goal is not to make every model perfectly predictable but to build systems that remain secure even when the model is not. “You should not have to choose between innovation and safety,” he said.
Article Summary: Microsoft is adding 35 types of local agents, bringing the total supported to 60. Sandboxes give agents policy-controlled access to resources. Microsoft plans to feed signals such as chain-of-thought into its risk scoring to spot when an agent’s plans diverge from its task.
