Article Title: American billionaire Mark Cuban strongly believes that manufacturing can return to the US from China; it is really simple, all that Americans need is ...
Article Text:
Mark Cuban: ‘Our robots and AI versus their robots and AI'

Cost plus drugs example

Palmer Luckey: High-cost claims are ‘psychological operations’

AI competition with China intensifies

American billionaire and Shark Tank judge Mark Cuban believes bringing manufacturing back to the United States is "really simple": outcompete China in robotics and artificial intelligence. The Shark Tank investor argued that advances in automation could make domestic production economically viable, reducing America's reliance on Asian manufacturing hubs. Cuban made the remarks in a post on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) on Sunday while responding to comments from Anduril Industries co-founder Palmer Luckey, who had pushed back against claims that manufacturing products in the United States is prohibitively expensive.Cuban framed the future of manufacturing as a technological race between the United States and China. "It's really simple. Our Robots and AI vs their Robots and AI," Cuban wrote. "If we can catch up on robotics/software, and can stay ahead on AI, there is zero reason manufacturing won't come back, or initiate here."According to Cuban, automation and software advances could help offset labour-cost advantages that have traditionally driven companies to manufacture products in China and other parts of Asia.The billionaire pointed to his pharmaceutical venture, Cost Plus Drugs, as an example of how domestic production could become competitive. Cuban said the company could manufacture generic medicines in Dallas at lower costs than importing them from Asia if not for various fees associated with bringing production online."At Cost Plus Drugs, the only thing holding us back from making generic drugs cheaper in Dallas than we can buy from Asia, are the fees we have to pay," he wrote.Luckey had said that stories about iPhones costing $37,000 or laptops costing $100,000 if made in the US are psychological operations. They are “sometimes pushed by foreign adversaries but more commonly by American corporations that want anything but an upset to the status quo,” he said.He added that companies that treat US manufacturing as impossible want to justify staying in China and avoid admitting “it is a choice.” Luckey also said a 30% tariff can bring production home only if making the product in the US costs less than 30% more.The discussion arrives amid growing competition between the US and China in artificial intelligence and advanced manufacturing technologies. Recent industry data cited by Reuters showed Nvidia held a 34% share of China's AI accelerator market during the first half of 2026, while Huawei's share rose to 28% as the Chinese technology giant gained ground in the sector.Chinese semiconductor companies have also continued expanding their capabilities in memory chips and AI infrastructure, increasing pressure on Western rivals. The strategic importance of AI was also highlighted by US President Donald Trump, who recently rejected the idea of a US-China AI joint venture, arguing that such cooperation could risk sharing sensitive technology with Beijing. "Whoever wins super intelligence wins," Trump said.
Article Summary: Shark Tank judge Mark Cuban believes the future of manufacturing is a technological race between the United States and China. Cuban made the remarks in a post on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) on Sunday. He was responding to comments from Anduril Industries co-founder Palmer Luckey, who had pushed back against claims that manufacturing products in the US is expensive.

Article Title: A California developer proposed a nearly 1 million-square-foot AI data centre beside homes, promising 1,600 construction jobs; residents fought back, and a judge has now required a full environmental
Article Text:
Judge sends project back to square one

Residents push back

Lawsuits and political fights

AI boom fuels race for data centre sites

Google link questioned

A California judge has ordered a complete environmental review of a proposed artificial intelligence data center in Imperial County. The judgement has marked a major victory for the local residents who have spent months fighting a project they believed could affect the water supply, increase emissions and also disrupt life in their community. The facility in question is backed by developer Sebastian Rucci through his company Imperial Valley Computer Manufacturing (IVCM). The facility is said to span nearly 1 millions square feet, making it to be one of the largest AI-focused data centres planned in California. As reported by Guardian, Rucci has argued that the project would help generate more than 1,600 construction jobs and nearly $30 million in annual tax revenue while helping in the establishment of an artificial intelligence infrastructure hub. But the project has now become a flashpoint in the growing national debate over the environmental impact of AI data centres.The data centre was approved by Imperial County earlier this year under an exemption from California's environmental review requirements. But following legal challenges from the City of Imperial and environmental groups, a county judge ruled that the project cannot proceed without undergoing a comprehensive environmental assessment.The decision effectively pauses development and requires officials to evaluate the facility's potential impact on water resources, electricity infrastructure, emissions and surrounding communities before construction can begin. Legal representatives for the City of Imperial said the review process could take a year or longer and would also require consideration of alternative locations.Residents say they only learned of the project from a flyer left on doors the day before Thanksgiving last year. Francisco Leal, whose home is across the street from the site, began texting neighbours. Nearly 3,500 people eventually signed a petition against the facility, and state senator Steve Padilla introduced a series of bills aimed at data centres.Residents cited fears of emissions, harm to wildlife such as the endangered desert pupfish, strain on the power grid, noise and scarce water. The centre would need about 750,000 gallons of water a day, Rucci says, drawn from a region that depends on the drought-stricken Colorado River. He denies the project will cause such harms and says its water use is equivalent to a 160-acre farm.“This project was presented as a Noah’s Ark that’s going to come save everybody,” Leal said. “But the community sees this project as a Trojan horse.”The area has the highest poverty rate in California, at close to 20%, and one in five adults is unemployed. “Communities are asking these questions of who benefits and who pays the price,” said Carla Walker of the World Resources Institute.Over the past year, more than half a dozen lawsuits have been filed, a temporary 45-day moratorium on data centres was approved, and a recall campaign targets county supervisor Peggy Price, who supported the project. That campaign is ongoing.The city of Imperial sued the county for bypassing public input and environmental review, and the Sierra Club later joined. Rucci’s company, Imperial Valley Computer Manufacturing, countersued in federal court and also sued the local irrigation district over a rejected water application. He filed defamation suits against an activist, a nonprofit and its director, and public-media station KPBS and a reporter. Those three suits were dismissed. He has appealed two of them and is working to reverse the third.At a March county meeting, protesters chanted “no datacenters” and Rucci left early. The county approved the project in April.The dispute highlights the increasing tension between communities and developers seeking land for AI infrastructure. The rapid growth of artificial intelligence services such as large language models has triggered a construction boom in data centres, which require vast amounts of computing power, electricity and cooling capacity.Developers are increasingly targeting rural and economically disadvantaged regions where large plots of land and power supplies are available. Imperial County, with its industrial zoning and access to significant electricity resources, became an attractive location despite concerns over scarce water resources and environmental sensitivity.According to Rucci, the project would eventually secure access to 330 megawatts of electricity, enough to power a sizeable city.Sebastian Rucci previously suggested the facility could support Google's AI ambitions, claiming to have secured interest from the technology giant for the project. Emails cited in the report indicated the proposed data centre could be used for AI and Gemini-related computing workloads.However, Google denied involvement in the Imperial County project and said it was not part of any data centre development in the area. Rucci acknowledged there was no formal agreement in place.
Article Summary: A California judge has ordered a complete environmental review of a proposed artificial intelligence data center in Imperial County. The judgement has marked a major victory for the local residents who have spent months fighting a project they believed could affect the water supply. The facility in question is backed by developer Sebastian Rucci through his company Imperial Valley Computer Manufacturing (IVCM) The facility is said to span nearly 1 millions square feet, making it to be one of the largest AI-focused data centres planned in California.

Article Title: Microsoft exits UK’s largest AI data centre project over power supply concerns
Article Text:
Data centre (Representative image)

Severe grid constraints cited as reason for exiting data centre project

Microsoft has reportedly terminated its agreement to participate in the flagship project to construct the United Kingdom’s largest artificial intelligence (AI) data centre, citing severe regional power constraints. However, British infrastructure firm Nscale, which announced the 2-billion-pounds facility in Loughton, Essex in 2025, has said that it remains committed to completing the project and is finding other ways to power the data centre. The project was by former Prime Minister Keir Starmer’s administration as the country's pre-eminent “sovereign AI” hub.Microsoft had previously intended to serve as the anchor tenant, with plans to fund and host a supercomputer at the site using part of its announced $30 billion (£22 billion) UK investment package. Despite Microsoft’s exit, which was first reported by The Telegraph and confirmed by the BBC, Nscale insisted it will complete the development and is actively looking for alternative ways to power the location.“We remain committed to both the Loughton project and the UK and we are exploring alternative power sources for the site, in addition to other expansion sites in the UK. Our relationship with Microsoft remains strong and long-term,” an Nscale spokesperson said.The collapse of the agreement follows growing anxiety over the site’s energy timeline. While the facility was initially scheduled to receive its primary electrical feed by the end of this year ahead of an opening next year, UK Power Networks (UKPN), which manages the regional electricity grid across London and the South East, reportedly notified Nscale that it would not be able to deliver sufficient electricity to the Loughton hub until the early to mid-2030s.The report also said that the multi-year connection delay proved insurmountable for Microsoft’s near-term supercomputing requirements. In response, Nscale said it has cleared the former scaffolding yard location, which had raised eyebrows earlier this year when The Guardian reported that industrial scaffolding operations were still active on-site, and is now exploring options to generate electricity directly on-site to bypass local grid logjams.The departure leaves Nscale without a publicly announced customer for the Essex development, putting unexpected pressure on the high-profile startup.
Article Summary: Microsoft has reportedly terminated its agreement to participate in the flagship project to construct the United Kingdom’s largest artificial intelligence (AI) data centre. British infrastructure firm Nscale, which announced the 2-billion- pounds facility in Loughton, Essex in 2025, has said that it remains committed to completing the project.

Article Title: In 2018, Steve and Connie Ballmer and the Clippers gave $10 million to restore Los Angeles basketball courts; four years later, the project finished renovations on 350 public courts across the city
Article Text:
In 2018, Steve and Connie Ballmer and the Clippers gave $10 million to restore Los Angeles basketball courts; four years later, the project finished renovations on 350 public courts across the city

Steve Ballmer: Project made basketball more accessible

In 2018, Los Angeles Clippers owner Steve Ballmer and his wife, Connie Ballmer, gave $10 million to renovate public basketball courts across Los Angeles. Four years later, the project reached its goal, with 350 courts refurbished across the city. The final renovated court was unveiled on June 28, 2022, at the Michelle and Barack Obama Sports Center in Los Angeles. Ballmer attended the event with then-Mayor Eric Garcetti, marking the completion of the Clippers Community Courts project.The Clippers had partnered with the Los Angeles Parks Foundation to renovate the courts. The Ballmers were initially approached in 2018 to help restore a select number of courts, but they decided to fund renovations across the city.“This was the largest donation ever to the City of Los Angeles’ parks system and it has transformed recreation centers, and been a point of pride, for nearly every neighborhood in the City,” said Carolyn Ramsay, the Los Angeles Parks Foundation’s executive director.Steve Ballmer said the project has made basketball courts more accessible to people across Los Angeles.“The City of L.A.'s population is almost 4 (million) people, and 98% of them live within two miles of a Clippers Community Court.That means 3.9 (million) people have access to these courts and all of the benefits that come with them," Ballmer said on Tuesday. "With our partners at the Los Angeles Parks Foundation and L.A.’s Department of Recreation and Parks, this is a proud achievement."The renovated facilities have also served purposes beyond sports. During the Covid-19 pandemic, some were used as shelters, emergency childcare centres and alternative learning sites. Ballmer said the project was aimed at making a difference in the lives of young people. The renovated courts are also expected to support youth sports in Los Angeles ahead of the 2028 Summer Olympics, which the city will host.“impact kids' lives... But if we get a few fans out of it, I’m good with that too," he said. He then added, "We're here to win championships, excite fans and help kids."
Article Summary: In 2018, Los Angeles Clippers owner Steve Ballmer and his wife, Connie Ballmer, gave $10 million to renovate public basketball courts. Four years later, the project reached its goal, with 350 courts refurbished across the city. The final renovated court was unveiled on June 28, 2022, at the Michelle and Barack Obama Sports Center.

Article Title: India’s smartphone shipments fall 26% to a decade-low third-quarter level despite festive season; Samsung regains top spot, powered by flagship phones: Report
Article Text: India's smartphone market shipments are estimated to have declined 26% year-on-year (YoY) to 35.8 million units in third quarter of 2026, marking their lowest third-quarter shipment volume since 2016 despite the start of the festive season, according to an Omdia report. As per Omdia Smartphone Market Pulse 3Q26, "Higher smartphone prices and cautious consumer spending weighed on replacement demand, prompting vendors to adopt conservative inventory strategies. Weakening online-focused shipments added to the pressure, while the later timing of Diwali amplified the quarterly contraction by shifting a significant portion of offline festive inventory build-up from September into October.""India's smartphone market is shifting from online-led shipment expansion during the festive period to more selective, channel-driven growth, challenging vendors' traditional volume strategies," said Sanyam Chaurasia, principal analyst at Omdia. "September, historically a critical inventory build-up period for major online sales events, saw weaker shipment momentum. Fewer exclusive launches, limited affordable SKUs and narrowing promotional differences reduced the online channel's traditional festive advantage.This has disproportionately affected Chinese OEMs, whose combined market share fell to approximately 68% in 3Q26 from 75% in 3Q25. In contrast, Samsung and Apple strengthened their positions through premium portfolios, strong consumer demand, established channel partnerships and structured upgrade programs."“Following a tough 2026, India's smartphone market is expected to decline by a further low-single-digit percentage in 2027, testing vendors' ability to revive replacement demand as higher prices and longer device lifecycles become structural challenges. Pricing pressures are likely to persist through at least 1H27, making compelling device experiences increasingly important in driving upgrades. As premiumization continues, vendors must move beyond incremental hardware improvements toward AI-led experiences that evolve from basic assistance to more proactive, personalized capabilities. According to Omdia’s User Innovation Readiness research, nearly four in ten respondents in India say useful AI capabilities could make them willing to pay more for a smartphone. Stronger channel partnerships, financing, trade-in and upgrade programs will be equally important in translating these innovations into purchases and reducing barriers to replacement,” concluded Chaurasia.Samsung regains top spot, followed by VivoSamsung regained the top spot for the first time since 1Q24, shipping 6.7 million units, supported by the Galaxy A07, A17 and A27. The Galaxy S26 series, new Z foldables and S26 FE broadened its higher-value portfolio, while bank cashback, exchange benefits and longer-tenure financing supported upgrades across price tiers.Vivo slipped to second place with shipments of 6.4 million units, down 34% YoY, the sharpest decline among the top five. Repeated price hikes disrupted channel inventory planning, while constrained entry-level supplies weakened competitiveness. Shipments were mainly supported by the Y11 5G and Y21 5G, while the returning S-series, led by the S2, also contributed to volumes.Oppo ranked third with shipments of 4.9 million units, down 24% YoY, as rising prices and cautious retailer stocking weighed on its core A-series volumes. The Reno16 series supported its premiumization strategy, with camera-led differentiation and financing offers helping sustain demand at higher price points.Xiaomi ranked fourth with shipments of 4.7 million units, down 28% YoY, as rising component costs forced trade-offs in pricing and RAM/storage configurations, weakening its traditional value proposition. The Redmi 15A and A7 supported shipment volumes, while the Redmi Note 17 series, POCO X8 and X8 Power contributed to its higher-value portfolio.Apple rounded out the top five with shipments of 3.9 million units, supported by channel stocking ahead of anticipated price hikes and sustained demand for the base iPhone 17 and 16 models amid the absence of a new base iPhone 18. The late-quarter launch of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max gained momentum, supported by bank cashback, exchange bonuses and flexible no-cost EMI schemes.
Article Summary: India's smartphone market shipments are estimated to have declined 26% year-on- year (YoY) to 35.8 million units in third quarter of 2026. Samsung regained the top spot for the first time since 1Q24, shipping 6.7 million units.

Article Title: In 2017, Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen pledged $30 million for housing in Seattle; three years later, the project opened with 95 affordable apartments and a support centre for families
Article Text:
The Gardner House in Seattle (Image credit: Paul G. Allen Family Foundation Photo)

Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen’s $30 million pledge backed by city funding

Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen donated $30 million in 2017 to help homeless families in Seattle find stable housing. Three years later, the project opened with 95 affordable apartments and a community centre offering support services to families. Called Gardner House, the development was built through a partnership between the Paul G. Allen Family Foundation, the City of Seattle and nonprofit organisation Mercy Housing Northwest. The project aimed to help families facing homelessness by combining affordable housing with services such as childcare, employment assistance and help finding permanent homes.Gardner House has 95 family-sized apartments. About half are reserved for families needing long-term housing support, while the remaining units offer affordable housing to people experiencing or at risk of homelessness. The ground floor houses the Allen Family Center, an 8,000-square-foot community hub that provides housing and employment assistance, childcare, and other services. Two apartments were also designed to serve as in-home daycare facilities for residents who wanted to work as childcare providers.By the time the centre opened, 94 of the 95 apartments had already been filled.The Paul G. Allen Family Foundation provided $30 million to build the development.The City of Seattle contributed another $5 million, while the project also received $10.7 million through a tax credit. The city's contribution followed a 2017 announcement by then-Mayor Ed Murray, who said the funding would support permanent housing for homeless families and children. At the time, the city said 1,684 families were waiting for housing in King County.The development, initially called the Mount Baker Family Housing and Resource Center, broke ground in 2018 near Seattle's Mount Baker light rail station.Paul Allen, who co-founded Microsoft with Bill Gates, supported several philanthropic efforts aimed at addressing homelessness in Seattle. He died in October 2018 from complications of non-Hodgkin's lymphoma. His sister, Jody Allen, took over management of his estate and continued the foundation's work.
Article Summary: Microsoft co-founder Paul Allen donated $30 million in 2017 to help homeless families in Seattle find stable housing. Three years later, the project opened with 95 affordable apartments and a community centre offering support services to families. Called Gardner House, the development was built through a partnership between the Paul G. Allen Family Foundation, the City of Seattle and Mercy Housing Northwest.

Article Title: As Americans vandalise Flock surveillance cameras across US, company announces new security features; here's what is changing
Article Text:
New safeguards announced by Flock

Reports of misuse

Critics say the changes fall short

Flock Safety, the maker of AI-powered licence plate recognition cameras used by thousands of law enforcement agencies across the US, has announced a series of new privacy and accountability measures amid increasing scrutiny over police misuse of its technology and growing public backlash against surveillance systems, according to a report by ABC News. The announcement comes as incidents of Americans vandalising Flock cameras have increased across several communities, while reports of officers allegedly using the company's surveillance network to stalk former partners and conduct unauthorised searches have fuelled concerns about privacy and oversight.* Case numbers required. Law enforcement users must label every search with a criminal case number.* Automatic review. Abnormal search activity will trigger an automatic review, and proactive lockouts for the users involved.* Shorter data retention. The default retention period drops to seven days from 30.* Limits on sharing. Data from Flock’s 120,000 cameras across the US can be shared by police departments with agencies nationwide. Cities will now be able to choose which types of offenses other agencies can search for through their cameras.CEO Garrett Langley gave an example in a blog post announcing the changes: “City A could allow City B to search its cameras only for a stolen vehicle, missing person, or violent crime while blocking searches related to immigration enforcement.”“These changes reflect years of work and deliberation,” Langley wrote. “They are not the end of that work, but simply the continuation of our commitment to both safety and privacy. We are not perfect, so we will keep listening, improving, and building a better standard for public safety technology together.”The announcement follows weeks of scrutiny over how police have used the system. Last week, The Washington Post reported that at least 50 officers had been accused, charged or convicted of using Flock’s system and other license plate readers to spy on people, in many cases stalking girlfriends or former partners. The Post said it has since confirmed more than a dozen additional cases. Two safeguards suggested in the Post’s story are among those Flock has now announced.Earlier this month, a North Carolina police officer was arrested for allegedly using Flock license plate readers to track her boyfriend’s ex-wife, police said. In Savannah, Georgia, six police department employees were fired in August over alleged misuse of Flock cameras, according to ABC affiliate WJCL.Langley said a tool called Audit Assistance, introduced 16 weeks ago to detect abnormal activity and flag it for review, has been associated with arrests of several law enforcement officers who allegedly abused the system. About one-third of customers have adopted it. It will become mandatory by the end of the year.The company also said it had fixed a problem discovered in December 2025, in which some of its AI-powered pan-tilt-zoom cameras were publicly accessible. “For a brief period of time, third parties were able to access live streams and footage from those cameras,” Langley wrote, blaming a network configuration error by a vendor. “We are accountable,” he said.Civil rights advocates say the measures do not go far enough. “While this measure contains some meaningful improvements, such as the shortened retention policy, ultimately it is the same ‘Just Trust Us’ policy with a fresh coat of paint,” said Tom Bowman, policy counsel at the Center for Democracy & Technology, in a statement to ABC News.“Flock is still asking thousands of police departments to police themselves, despite evidence from across the U.S. that this lack of guardrails is unsafe,” he said. He argued that the changes do not address the risks of license plate readers, including pervasive tracking, vehicle stops based on flawed AI flags of “irregular” driving patterns, and stalking. The real fix, he said, is to “make the government get a warrant. ”The Institute for Justice, a libertarian nonprofit law firm, launched a database on Tuesday documenting abuse of automated license plate readers (ALPRs). It says it has found more than 100 incidents, including stalking, wrongful stops and detentions, and non-law enforcement use. The group says companies like Flock “have now blanketed thousands of communities with ALPRs,” creating systems that can reconstruct where people have been without a warrant.Flock’s name has become shorthand for ALPRs, which are marketed as tools for catching car thieves and finding missing people, although other companies also make them.
Article Summary: Flock Safety has announced a series of new privacy and accountability measures. Comes amid increasing scrutiny over police misuse of its technology. Reports of officers allegedly using the company's surveillance network to stalk former partners and conduct unauthorised searches have fuelled concerns about privacy and oversight.

Article Title: Users claims Meta smartglasses recording them in 'Sleep Mode', say have 'forgotten' the magic words to alert
Article Text:
Meta Ray-Ban Smart Glasses

Users claim unprompted lights and saved transcripts

Other owners quickly echoed the experience:

Meta says the ‘glitch has been fixed’

Privacy alarms are sounding once again for Meta’s smart glasses. Some wearers of Meta’s smart glasses are claiming that the connected eyewear has been recording private conversations and saving transcripts even while the hardware is supposed to be in “sleep mode” – all without hearing the required wake word. Citing three separate Reddit discussion threads, New York Post reports that multiple customers claimed that several iterations of the tech-enabled frames, which allow hands-free communication, audio playback, and video capture, have activated unexpectedly and captured ambient speech without user consent.The complaints center on the eyewear’s voice-trigger mechanism. Normally, wearers must say the prompt phrase “Hey Meta” to wake the glasses and engage the onboard assistant. However, owners say the devices have started bypassing that safeguard altogether following a recent firmware update.One wearer reported documenting the unprompted behaviour across three different pairs of Ray-Ban Meta glasses, covering both second- and third-generation units.“I have observed the same behavior on THREE different pairs of Ray-Ban Meta glasses, including 2nd- and 3rd-generation models. Meta AI does not respond to me, and I never intentionally activated it.I have noticed the white notification light activating while I am speaking normally,” the user wrote, explaining that the glasses began recording conversations with a friend without being prompted.The user added that the companion Meta AI application went so far as to store both audio recordings and written transcripts of those private discussions directly inside their conversation history logs. The owner noted they are preparing to pursue a class-action lawsuit if evidence shows the glitch is widespread.One user reported that resetting the hardware did not solve the problem: “I could see the LED light up in instances where I didn’t invoke Hey Meta.”A second owner noted silent activations: “Mine randomly activates the internal light now without any input from me. It does not make the wake-up noise voice command would the internal light just turns on. Something weird is going on!”Another user confirmed the same pattern on older hardware: “I made a post about the AI turning on during random conversations. It’s not just you. I have gen 2.”When contacted regarding the unprompted activations and phantom recordings, Meta did not explain the technical root cause behind the behaviour, but claimed the glitch has been handled.“This issue has been resolved. People can manage, review and delete voice logs of their interactions with Meta AI via settings at any time,” a Meta company spokesperson told The Post.
Article Summary: Users claim unprompted lights and saved transcripts on Meta Ray-Ban smart glasses. Glasses allow hands-free communication, audio playback, and video capture. Wearers must say the prompt phrase “Hey Meta” to wake the glasses and engage the onboard assistant.

Article Title: Larry Ellison loses $6 billion in a day, as AI worries wipe billions from Oracle stock, making it one of the worst-performing ...
Article Text:
Oracle founder Larry Ellison

AI bets and debt concerns weigh on Oracle

Infrastructure projects face regulatory hurdles

Core business remains resilient

Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison saw his fortune shrink by more than $6 billion in a single day as investors continued to dump Oracle shares amid growing concerns over the company's artificial intelligence investments, rising debt burden and challenges facing key data centre projects. According to Bloomberg Billionaires Index data cited by Benzinga, Ellison's net worth fell by $6.1 billion on Friday, taking his estimated wealth to $178 billion. Over the past 12 months, the Oracle co-founder has reportedly lost about $194 billion in wealth, making him one of the biggest losers among the world's richest individuals.The decline in Ellison's fortune comes as Oracle stock has emerged as one of the worst-performing large technology companies on Wall Street. Shares have plunged about 62% from their peak, wiping roughly $550 billion off the company's market value. Oracle's market capitalisation has fallen from approximately $875 billion late last year to around $387 billion.Investor concerns have centred on Oracle's aggressive push into artificial intelligence infrastructure and its growing debt obligations. The company has attracted scrutiny over its exposure to OpenAI-related projects, including a reported $300 billion agreement linked to the Stargate initiative.At the same time, Oracle's total debt has surged to $169 billion from $88 billion early last year, raising concerns about future financing costs.The pressure has also spread to Oracle's bond market performance. Bonds maturing in 2036 are now yielding 7.8%, significantly higher than the year's low of 5.3%, while another $2.75 billion in bonds maturing in 2066 are yielding 8.73%, reflecting investor demands for greater compensation to hold the company's debt.Oracle is also grappling with challenges surrounding Project Jupiter, its major data centre development in New Mexico. The company has reportedly declared force majeure on the project, citing power supply and gas pipeline constraints. In July, the New Mexico State Land Office rejected the proposed Green Chile pipeline permit, pointing to concerns over water consumption, carbon emissions and limited economic benefits for the state. The project is also facing separate air-quality permitting issues.Despite the market's concerns, Oracle's underlying business continues to post strong growth driven by demand for cloud services.In its latest quarterly results, the company reported a 30% increase in revenue to $19.3 billion. Cloud infrastructure revenue surged 121% to $7.4 billion, while cloud applications revenue reached $4.2 billion. Oracle's remaining performance obligations, a key indicator of future revenue, climbed to $664 billion.Analysts expect that momentum to continue. After generating $67 billion in revenue in the previous fiscal year, Oracle is projected to deliver about $90 billion this year and $117 billion next year. Earnings per share are forecast to rise from $7.63 last year to $8.14 this year.
Article Summary: Ellison's net worth fell by $6.1 billion on Friday, taking his estimated wealth to $178 billion. Oracle stock has emerged as one of the worst-performing large technology companies on Wall Street. Oracle's market capitalisation has fallen from approximately $875 billion late last year to around $387 billion.

Article Title: From bookings to handwritten notes, Apple's Siri finds a way into Indian apps
Article Text:
Apple's Siri

Getting the best out of Siri

New Delhi: Finding a contract, checking a movie booking or searching handwritten notes no longer necessarily requires opening an app and navigating its menus. Indian developers are integrating their services with Apple ’s upgraded Siri, allowing users to describe what they need and retrieve information or trigger actions through voice commands.In case you were wondering what the fuss over new Siri is, then here’s a quick update: Siri AI is Apple’s upgraded voice assistant, designed to understand conversational requests and use context from what users are viewing. Apple has connected it more closely with apps, allowing developers to make searches, information and actions accessible through Siri. Instead of remembering a fixed command, users can describe what they want or refer to something on screen.District, Glance, Noteshelf, Signeasy and Mood Dial are among the apps adopting these capabilities. Their developers say the change goes beyond earlier Siri integrations, which typically required preset commands or Shortcuts. Users can now make conversational requests and refer to information already displayed on their screens.“Earlier, users had to set up Shortcuts or remember specific phrases to trigger an action,” said Rama Krishna, founder of Fluid Touch, which develops Noteshelf.In Noteshelf, users can ask where they wrote about a Chennai trip, seek an explanation of a diagram or request a summary to be added to an existing note. The integration makes handwritten material accessible through these requests.“Siri also understands what’s on screen, even handwritten notes, so users can ask questions about their notes and add the answers back in,” Krishna said.The same shift is taking place in document management. Signeasy users can retrieve a named contract, check documents awaiting signatures or ask Siri to open an item from the list on screen.“Earlier, Siri could open Signeasy or run a fixed Shortcut, and that was about it,” said Santhosh J, head of mobile at Signeasy.Making these actions available required developers to rethink how their apps function. Apple’s App Intents framework lets them expose individual capabilities—such as searching, retrieving information or creating content—to the operating system. An action previously tied to a particular screen must work independently.“That made us separate what the app does from how it looks,” Santhosh said. A small team built Signeasy’s integration alongside regular releases, with document-related actions accessible through multiple entry points.For consumer apps, that approach creates another route to discovery. District, part of Eternal, lets users search for experiences and retrieve information about dining, movie and event bookings.“Users can discover experiences within District through Siri’s Search in App and Visual Intelligence,” said Adarsh Singh, software development engineer at District.The company exposed its search capabilities and booking data through App Intents. “It also shifted our approach towards making District’s experiences accessible beyond the app itself,” Singh said.Glance is using Siri to deliver shopping recommendations based on preferences including style, fit, budget and favourite brands. Users can see recommendations in Siri’s response or continue browsing in Glance.“The integration took more than 10 weeks of coordinated effort between Glance’s product and technology teams and Apple’s WWDR India team,” said Arvind Jayaprakash, senior vice-president, technology, Glance.However, discovery does not extend to completing a purchase. “Glance helps users discover products that match their preferences, but it doesn’t complete purchases on their behalf,” Jayaprakash said. Users are directed to merchants to review products and pay.For Mood Dial, a music app for Apple Music subscribers, conversational requests replace the need to remember a station’s exact name.“Now you can just say how you feel,” said founder Mohit Nandwani. A request for music suited to a quiet, rainy night can select an existing station or initiate the creation of another.The integration also required a less obvious adjustment: reducing Siri’s spoken responses. “I took the talking out,” Nandwani said, explaining that speech after playback begins pauses the music. Clear requests therefore start playback silently; ambiguous ones prompt clarification.Whether these interactions generate additional business remains unclear. District reported 1,897 successful Visual Intelligence fetches, 329 Search in App queries and 287 booking lookups. It did not specify the measurement period or unique-user count. These are interactions, not completed bookings. Glance, Noteshelf and Signeasy have not shared usage figures.Availability also varies. Most developers described English support on compatible Apple Intelligence devices, with newer capabilities tied to iOS 27. Older, fixed Siri commands can remain available separately. District said its Visual Search supports Hindi and English.Data handling differs by action. Noteshelf says it uses on-device processing and makes notebook information searchable through Spotlight. Signeasy says its contract summaries use Apple’s on-device Foundation Models, keeping document content on the phone.Mood Dial says matching a request to an existing station happens locally. Creating a new station sends the user’s sentence to its server under an anonymous identifier, with confirmation required before creation. Health data is excluded from Siri requests.Consequential actions retain additional steps. Signeasy requires signing within the app and manual review before sending through Mail; Glance leaves checkout to merchants. Developers have opened new routes into their services, but have yet to demonstrate whether users will regularly choose them over tapping through an app. Can the new and improved Siri AI become a daily habit for users? If app developers continue integrating it and expand on its use cases, then perhaps that's a possibility.
Article Summary: Indian developers are integrating their services with Apple ’s upgraded Siri. Users can describe what they need and retrieve information or trigger actions through voice commands. District, Glance, Noteshelf, Signeasy and Mood Dial are among the apps adopting these capabilities.

Article Title: UK to scrap the non-compete rule that kept Google DeepMind researchers on paid year-long breaks; PM Andy Burnham says: Some businesses have gone...
Article Text:
UK plans to end non-competes that kept some Google DeepMind staff away from rivals for up to a year

The UK has not yet said how far its non-compete ban will go

Google DeepMind used non-competes to keep AI talent away from rivals

DeepMind's top researchers are leaving London for Anthropic and OpenAI

The UK government plans to legislate against non-compete clauses, the contract terms that stop employees from joining a rival or starting a company for months after they quit. Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced the move in Manchester on October 9, and it lands squarely on one of Britain's most prized tech employers, Google DeepMind.Some DeepMind staff in London have reportedly been barred from working for competitors for up to 12 months after leaving. Many sit out that period on garden leave, drawing full pay from Google while doing no work for it. With Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta hiring aggressively in London, those clauses have become a sore point for researchers and for the startups trying to hire them."I believe some businesses have gone too far in their use of restrictive practices such as non-compete clauses," Burnham said. "That's a drag on innovation and prevents the best really being energized and bringing that dynamism to the economy."AI minister Kanishka Narayan said on X that the government will also look at other restrictive practices, such as excessive notice periods. "We want people to have the freedom to move to a better job and help our most promising businesses grow," he wrote.The finer details are still open. When Keir Starmer's government set out options in November 2025, they ranged from a total ban to a partial one, such as allowing non-competes only above a salary threshold or capping how long they can last.The final shape is expected to be worked out with industry.The push gained pace last month when 20 founders signed an open letter calling for an end to non-competes, long notice periods and garden leave. The letter came from Inherent Labs, an AI startup founded by former DeepMind staff. Founders and investors have long argued that California, which does not enforce non-competes, has a clear edge in hiring.At DeepMind, the length of a non-compete has reportedly depended on a person's seniority and how critical their work is. Six months was common, including for engineers working on Gemini, while some senior researchers got a full year. Google has said its contracts are in line with market standards and that it uses non-competes selectively.Former DeepMind director Nando de Freitas, now a vice-president at Microsoft AI, said last year that DeepMind employees reached out to him every week asking how to escape their notice periods and non-competes.For Google, the change arrives in the middle of a run of high-profile exits. Nobel laureate John Jumper, who co-led AlphaFold, is moving to Anthropic but is not expected to start until next year, a delay that lines up with the cooling-off periods UK non-competes impose. Gemini researchers Jonas Adler and Alexander Pritzel have also left for Anthropic, while Noam Shazeer joined OpenAI after more than two decades at Google.Figures from UK-based Zeki Data show DeepMind's share of research hires across Europe, the Middle East and Africa fell from 49% in 2022-23 to 18.6% in 2025-26. Anthropic was the top destination for those who left.Not everyone backs the change. Financial services lobby group TheCityUK opposed a ban earlier this year, arguing that non-competes are often the only way to protect confidential information and intellectual property.
Article Summary: UK plans to end non-competes that kept some Google DeepMind staff away from rivals for up to a year. Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced the move in Manchester on October 9. The final shape is expected to be worked out with industry. For Google, the change arrives in the middle of a run of high-profile exits.

Article Title: This US AI lab offers free plumbing, electrical work and other tasks in three cities but there is a catch: Workers will wear sensors that…
Article Text:
Representative image

‘Web-scraped data no longer enough’

‘Capturing unpredictable real-world work’

An AI laboratory specialising in real-world data collection is offering homeowners free home repairs and maintenance services across three major US cities. However, the program comes with a specific condition: the technicians sent to do the job will wear sensors to record their movements to collect data that will be used to train the next generation of AI-powered robots. The startup, called HUMXN, announced that it will fully subsidise essential trade services, including plumbing, electrical work, HVAC repairs, air-duct cleaning and carpet cleaning.As per a report by Tom’s Hardware, under the arrangement, residents who need repairs can receive qualified services at no financial cost. In exchange, they must agree to allow trade professionals outfitted with “wearable capture technology” into their homes to record how they perform complex, physical tasks on-site.The push into home comes as tech companies have reportedly understood that digital text, web photos and online video clips are insufficient for teaching physical machines how to operate in everyday environments.“The next generation of AI is going to need more than text and images from the internet. Robots need to understand how skilled people interact with the physical world. Home-service technicians perform millions of highly technical tasks every day.We are creating a way for homeowners and service companies to benefit financially from the value of that expertise,” said HUMXN founder Thomas Unise.Unise noted that while millions of trade specialists execute sophisticated mechanical operations daily, virtually none of that practical knowledge is cataloged in digital formats that machine-learning models can process.“We want to build the infrastructure that connects that knowledge with the companies building the next generation of intelligent machines while making sure the people creating the value participate in the economics,” Unise added.According to HUMXN, attempting to recreate the natural, instinctive motions of skilled laborers inside artificial laboratory environments is difficult. By sending technicians into actual residences, the company can record authentic workflows across diverse housing layouts, varied equipment types, unique structural problems, individual technician styles and different environmental conditions.The recorded sensor telemetry will provide AI models with detailed, step-by-step insight into how experienced technicians solve problems in real time. This includes inspecting physical fixtures and diagnosing malfunctions; testing active home systems; selecting the proper tools for specific scenarios; adapting to changing physical conditions on the job, and verifying that a repair has been completed successfully and safely.The company is rolling out the initiative across three select markets chosen to capture operational data across sharply different regional climates: Chicago, Minneapolis and Miami. Residents living in those three metropolitan areas can verify their eligibility by visiting the official HUMXN Free Home Service webpage.
Article Summary: HUMXN is offering free home repairs and maintenance services across three major US cities. In exchange, technicians will wear sensors to record their movements to collect data that will be used to train the next generation of AI-powered robots. The company is rolling out the initiative across three select markets chosen to capture operational data across sharply different regional climates.

Article Title: Jefferies' Chris Wood has a warning on what BlackRock's Larry Fink said is saving America from recession; says: There is also a growing realisation that China has …
Article Text:
Blackrock CEO Larry Fink

Why Jefferies' Chris Wood is worried about America's AI spending

Why Larry Fink says stopping data centre construction could hurt the US economy

What this may means for US economy

BlackRock CEO Larry Fink recently warned that a halt to data centre construction in the US could push the country into a recession, saying the economy increasingly depends on spending on artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure. Now, Jefferies' global head of equity strategy, Chris Wood, has raised concerns about the same investment boom, warning that cheaper Chinese AI models could threaten the returns American companies expect from their massive spending. The two views highlight a growing debate over the future of the AI boom. While Fink believes continued investment in data centres is essential to economic growth, Wood has warned that the money pouring into AI infrastructure could lead to massive capital destruction in the US if companies fail to earn enough from their investments.Wood's concern comes as major technology companies continue to spend billions of dollars on AI chips, computing facilities and the power systems needed to run them. Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft and Meta are expected to spend more than $720 billion on capital expenditure this year, according to analyst estimates compiled by Bloomberg.Jefferies' Chris Wood has warned that the AI boom could destroy significant amounts of capital in the US over the long term.The scale of the spending helps explain the concern. As mentioned above, Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft and Meta are expected to spend more than $720 billion on capital expenditure this year, with much of it going towards AI infrastructure.Alphabet alone expects to spend between $195 billion and $205 billion in 2026, more than double the $91.4 billion it spent in 2025. Alphabet President and Chief Investment Officer Ruth Porat has also indicated that the company plans to spend "significantly more" in 2027.But the investment is increasingly being funded through debt, including loans from private credit funds. Outstanding private loans to AI-related companies have risen to more than $200 billion by some estimates. Even Alphabet reported negative free cash flow in the second quarter for the first time since its 2004 initial public offering, while its long-term debt reached about $98 billion at the end of June, more than four times the level a year earlier.The bigger concern for Wood is whether companies will be able to earn enough from AI to justify this spending. Wood has argued that Chinese models could turn large language models into a commodity, making it harder for US companies to recover the enormous costs of developing and running them. He has also said China "has become a technological peer to the U.S. in AI."Larry Fink, on the other hand, has recently warned that a halt to data centre construction could have consequences well beyond the technology sector. Speaking to CNBC after BlackRock reported its third-quarter earnings, he said, “If we have a moratorium of some sort in this country, we will be in a recession.”“So much of our economy is based on the buildout of this capex,” he added, referring to capital expenditure on AI infrastructure.Data centres require spending on buildings, computing hardware and energy systems. This creates work for construction companies, equipment suppliers and businesses involved in power infrastructure. Fink argues that stopping new projects could therefore affect jobs and economic activity across several industries.Fink further argued that the economic benefits of building more AI capacity outweigh the concerns. Speaking at the Milken Institute Global Conference in May, he said, "I don't believe we're moving fast enough," while dismissing concerns about an AI bubble."There is not an AI bubble. There is the opposite. We have supply shortages. Demand is growing much faster than anyone has ever anticipated — and this is just a U.S. phenomenon,” he added.Fink and Wood are looking at different sides of the same investment boom. Fink believes that AI infrastructure spending supports jobs and economic growth, while Wood warns that the spending could destroy capital if the technology becomes cheaper and the returns fall short of expectations.Both outcomes could matter for the wider economy. A sharp slowdown in data centre construction could affect industries that depend on the investment. But if companies borrow heavily to build AI infrastructure and fail to earn enough from it, the losses could spread to investors and lenders.For now, major technology companies are showing little sign of pulling back. Alphabet's Porat said, "You must invest for long term growth," adding, "By the time you need it, it’s too late to say, OK, now we’re going to start."The question is whether demand for AI will grow quickly enough to justify the enormous sums being spent, especially as Chinese models offer cheaper alternatives. That tension sits at the heart of the debate over whether America's AI boom will sustain economic growth or leave companies facing costly investments that fail to pay off.
Article Summary: Jefferies' Chris Wood has warned that the AI boom could destroy significant amounts of capital in the US over the long term. Larry Fink, on the other hand, has argued that a halt to data centre construction could have consequences well beyond the technology sector. Fink believes that AI infrastructure spending supports jobs and economic growth, while Wood warns that the spending could destroy capital.

Article Title: Charles Schwab is blocking AI Agents, CEO Rick Wurster asks the 'money question' that almost every bank in America is asking: Who will be responsible if ...
Article Text:
Charles Schwab is blocking AI Agents, CEO Rick Wurster asks the 'money question' that almost every bank in America is asking: Who will be responsible if ...

Charles Schwab CEO makes it clear that AI Agents cannot be 'trusted completely'

American banks and financial institutions seem to be waking up to the AI threat, or should we say rogue AI threat. Charles Schwab has begun actively blocking third-party Artificial Intelligence (AI) agents from moving client funds, Chief Executive Rick Wurster said in an interview, highlighting growing Wall Street anxiety over autonomous software managing real money. The restriction specifically targets outside AI agents—including Meta’s new personal assistant, Muse—that attempt to execute financial transactions after users supply them with account credentials.“We can’t control it, the client can’t control it, something could go wrong and who’s liable?” Wurster told Bloomberg Television. The CEO pointed to an unsettled regulatory landscape where U.S. lawmakers have yet to define clear liability standards for autonomous AI actions.Wurster noted that he reviews weekly security logs showing unauthorized agent attempts being intercepted in the "tens and twenties" each week. Meta’s Muse, designed to autonomously negotiate, purchase, and book services for users, is among the tools being turned away at Schwab’s digital gates.Rather than permitting outside bots broad operational access, Schwab is deploying controlled Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.The standard acts as a secure bridge, permitting vetted third-party AI models to pull balance inquiries and market research without granting transactional clearance. For hands-on account management, Schwab is steering customers toward Charley, its proprietary, in-house assistant launched late last month.America's leading brokerage is not alone in its anti-AI stance. The defensive stance adopted by Charles Schwab reflects an industry-wide pivot toward containment. Earlier this week, JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon sounded a similar alarm on an earnings call, warning investors of potential “rogue agents” and affirming that the nation’s largest bank will not permit external autonomous software to initiate wire transfers or settle bills.The crackdowns arrive as financial regulators across the United States and Europe step up scrutiny of generative AI integration in banking. Even the restricted bridges carry risks; tech and financial heavyweights, including Google and JPMorgan, recently patched vulnerabilities discovered within MCP-style connection architectures. For now, major institutions are making their boundary clear: AI Algorithms are welcome to read the ledger, but we cannot give them the keys.
Article Summary: Charles Schwab has begun actively blocking third-party Artificial Intelligence (AI) agents from moving client funds. The restriction specifically targets outside AI agents that attempt to execute financial transactions after users supply them with account credentials. JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon sounded a similar alarm on an earnings call, warning investors of potential 'rogue agents'

Article Title: San Francisco techie shuts down video game that had players killing 'homeless people'; says: Made a personal donation to …
Article Text:
Developer says the game was built using AI tools

A San Francisco tech developer has apologized for creating a video game that turned the city’s notorious Tenderloin neighborhood into a zombie-killing zone. “Targeting people struggling with addiction or homelessness was never my intention” Pierre-Louis Biojout @plbiojout wrote in a post on X (formerly Twitter), further adding that he has taken down the game. The development comes after critics of the game argued that it allowed players to target homeless drug users. In addition to shutting down the game, the developer said that he has refunded all advertisers and also made a personal donation to a drug treatment and recovery service.“I built and posted a zombie game set on San Francisco streets. The setting and the way I promoted it showed poor judgment. Targeting people struggling with addiction or homelessness was never my intention,” the techie said.“I’ve taken the game and promotional posts down, refunded all advertisers, and made a personal donation to treatment and recovery services by Delancey Street equal to the game’s total revenue,” he further added.Pierre-Louis Biojout released a free, multiplayer browser game last week, describing it as a “Call of Duty style zombie shooter on the real SF streets.” The developer claimed that he built the game in just one weekend using the AI tools.He further revealed that he had taken $300 in advertising revenue.However, critics soon called out the game. “You think you’re being edgy but you’re just a huge piece of s–t,” one person wrote on social media. “Bring back shame. This is atrocious PR,” another fumed.City Supervisor Bilal Mahmood, who represents the Tenderloin told the San Francisco Chronicle: “Turning violence against real people, including unhoused people, into entertainment is dehumanizing and should never be normalized”.

Article Title: Elon Musk to Dario Amodei: I do not agree with your donation of Anthropic shares; I recommend …
Article Text:
Anthropic to allocate 5% of shares to public benefit fund

Anthropic has announced to donate a portion of the company’s shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new wholly owned entity dedicated entirely to the public benefit. In a post on X (formerly known as Twitter), the Claude-maker said that it will start with giving away 5% of shares. “For every 50% increase in the company’s value over a set baseline, we can contribute up to an extra 2%, subject to our board’s discretion,” the company, led by Dario Amodei said. “In total, this means that roughly 20% of Anthropic’s shares are committed to the public good. Our co-founders have already pledged to donate 80% of their equity, and around half our employees are donating a portion of their equity as part of a donation matching program we’ve run since our founding,” the post continues. Elon Musk replied to Anthropic’s announcement recommending shares be distributed directly to the public instead of routed through an intermediary entity. “I recommend giving the shares directly to the public,” Elon Musk wrote. “This is what I will be doing,” he said in another post.Here’s the full announcement made by Anthropic"Today, we’re committing a portion of Anthropic’s shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new entity with a structure that increases the stake as the company grows.Subject to stockholder approval, 5% of Anthropic’s shares will be committed today, with an additional 2% added at the board’s discretion for every 50% increase in the company’s value above a set baseline.As a public benefit corporation, most of our work in pursuit of our mission takes place inside the company: research relevant to AI safety and interpretability; applied biomedical research; discounts on Claude for nonprofits and scientific institutions. These activities have both a public benefit component and for-profit value, so we house them directly in the company.The Anthropic Public Benefit Fund will have increased flexibility and scale, enabling us to pursue our mission in new ways: for example, we might explore large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations.One example is labor market impacts. AI may generate enormous economic value, but it could also cause instability for many workers. Anthropic has already committed $200 million to studying and addressing this issue, but given the pace of AI progress, bolder approaches may be needed. The Fund will have the versatility to pursue them.We’re establishing the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund as a wholly-owned LLC—rather than a 501(c)(3) or other format—to give adjustability between different forms of giving. None of the Anthropic equity held by the LLC will be used for lobbying or political giving, in the US or abroad.Because of the way the Fund is structured, the more Anthropic grows, the larger the share of the company that can be dedicated expressly to the public good. It is common practice for tech companies to offer escalating compensation awards to their executives. We are instead directing that equity to the public benefit.This builds on commitments our co-founders and employees have already made. When Anthropic was founded, our co-founders pledged to donate 80% of their equity holdings, and since founding we have also operated an equity donation match program that allows employees to pledge equity which Anthropic matches. Approximately half of our employees participate in this program. When combined with today’s announcement, roughly 20% of Anthropic shares will be dedicated to the public good, plus any additional percentage that could be added if the company reaches specific valuation milestones.In the coming months, we will share more about the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund’s structure and governance, including the valuation milestones that may add to its stake. We will also report on our progress to date against our mission in an upcoming public benefit report."
Article Summary: Anthropic to allocate 5% of shares to public benefit fund. Elon Musk replied to Anthropic’s announcement recommending shares be distributed directly to the public. Anthropic has already committed $200 million to studying and addressing this issue, but given the pace of AI progress, bolder approaches may be needed.

Article Title: Meta’s ‘highest-paid employee’ Alexandr Wang on the WhatsApp message from Mark Zuckerberg that changed his career: Have time for a...
Article Text:
Meta AI chief Alexander Wang with CEO Mark Zuckerberg

Alexandr Wang's memo told Zuckerberg to hire fewer, better people

Meta's CFO warned Wang the AI bet had to work

Muse and Muse Wonder have put Meta back in the AI race

In April 2025, Alexandr Wang was sitting in a staff meeting at Scale AI, the data-labelling company he co-founded, when his phone pinged. It was a WhatsApp message from Mark Zuckerberg : "Have time for a call?" Wang's first thought, as he tells it now, was simply, "huh, interesting."That call ran for 44 minutes. Within two months, Meta had put $14.3 billion into Scale AI for a 49% stake and brought Wang in to run its AI efforts. Wang and Zuckerberg retold the story together on Cheeky Pint, the podcast hosted by Stripe co-founder John Collison, in an episode recorded around the release of Meta's new Muse Wonder AI model.The timing of that message matters. Meta had released its Llama 4 models on April 4, 2025, to a lukewarm response. Around April 20, Zuckerberg said, he started calling people across the industry for advice on what to do next. Wang was one of them.Two days after the call, Wang sent Zuckerberg a long memo. Zuckerberg described it on Cheeky Pint as Wang laying out what he would do "if I were in your position."The first point was about people, and how few of them Meta needed. "The very first thing is that you don't need a lot of people, and talent density is the thing that matters," Zuckerberg recalled.That idea still shapes Meta Superintelligence Labs. Its core research team numbers under 200, "closer to 100," according to Wang, inside a company of roughly 75,000 employees.The hire raised eyebrows. Wang, now 29, is an MIT dropout who built Scale AI into a key data supplier for the big AI labs, but he had never trained a frontier model. Collison pointed this out on the show. Zuckerberg said he spoke to the heads of research at all the major labs before deciding, and came away sure: "Alex is the guy."What followed was a recruiting sprint Zuckerberg called "supernova." He cleared his calendar for a month or two just to meet researchers. "I don't think either of us slept that much for the first couple of months," he said.Wang also recalled one early meeting that left him uneasy. When he said Meta's first priority should be a strong reasoning model, one of the existing leads asked whether consumers needed one at all. Wang said he called Nat Friedman, now head of Meta's AI products, straight after.By the end of 2025, the numbers had become enormous. Zuckerberg said Meta was preparing to "write this check for like, I don't know, like $100 billion, $200 billion" before anyone had seen the new models. "I'm like, Alex, are you sure this is going to work?"At an executive gathering in Hawaii, Wang said, CFO Susan Li pulled him aside several times to drive the point home. "If it's good, it's all good. We're great. But if it's bad, it's really, really, really bad." Wang admitted that all he had to show at the time was a "vibe report" on research progress and a few plots.The bet produced Muse Spark in April 2026, followed by the Muse personal agent app on September 8. Muse climbed to the top of Apple's App Store within days. Wang's own Muse, which he named Oiler, buys increasingly obscure teas from farms in Taiwan and Japan every week. Zuckerberg uses his to critique his MMA technique in the one-minute breaks between rounds.On October 12, Meta released Muse Wonder, the first model it calls frontier-class. For now, it sits behind paid Muse subscriptions. Zuckerberg said the team was "very, very critical" of its own work along the way, and Wang describes the lab as a room full of "insecure overachievers."Asked what kind of boss Zuckerberg is, Wang called him "very Bayesian," someone who updates his beliefs and then moves the whole company to match. A five-word WhatsApp message, and the 44-minute call that followed, is about as clear an example of that as Meta has.
Article Summary: Alexandr Wang was brought in by Mark Zuckerberg to run Meta's AI efforts. Wang and Zuckerberg retold the story on Cheeky Pint, the podcast hosted by Stripe co- founder John Collison. The bet produced Muse Spark in April 2026, followed by the Muse personal agent app.

Article Title: As investors debate if Accenture will be a winner or loser from AI, the company may be planning to say 'goodbye' to China, after receiving unsolicited ...

As investors debate if Accenture will be a winner or loser from AI, the company may be planning to say 'goodbye' to China, after receiving unsolicited ...

Accenture stock has seen ups and down this year

How billions from 'China office' sale may help

According to a report in Financial Times, 'Chinese operations' sale talks come as the world’s largest publicly traded IT consultancy Accenture sharpens its focus on faster-growing markets and seeks to reassure investors over its strategy in the artificial intelligence era.The Dublin-headquartered company has enlisted JPMorgan to conduct a strategic review of the unit following unsolicited approaches over the past year, according to people familiar with the matter cited by the Financial Times. Accenture may choose to maintain a meaningful minority holding to preserve continuity for existing multinational and domestic clients, though discussions remain preliminary and may not result in a final transaction.The strategic deliberations coincide with broader volatility for Accenture's stock, as markets evaluate whether consultancy giants will benefit from companies adoption artificial intelligence or suffer as clients automate internal workflows previously handled by external contractors.Meanwhile, tightening data security and cross-border regulatory scrutiny in Beijing has prompted several Western advisory firms, including McKinsey, to scale back their Chinese footprints, segregate technology infrastructure, and navigate hurdles to international integration.The potential divestment would provide fresh capital as Accenture positions itself for long-term artificial intelligence deployment.
